newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian premier flies to blast site--agencies.
newsitem.headline: Russian premier flies to blast site--agencies.

text.p: Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin flew on Sunday to the southern Russian town where a weekend blast destroyed a block of flats, killing or trapping many residents, Russian news agencies said.

Itar-Tass news agency said Chernomyrdin took off on Sunday morning for Kaspiysk in the Dagestan region, where rescue workers had dug 55 people from the ruins, 16 of them dead. About 40 people remained trapped in the ruins, Tass said.
Other Russian news reports earlier put the death toll from the Saturday morning blast, which officials say was probably caused by a bomb, at between 13 and 32.
Rescue workers were called in to try to pull survivors from the rubble of the eight-storey block, which housed mainly military personnel and their families.
They worked through the night on Saturday and into Sunday, which was declared a day of mourning in Dagestan, a region that borders the Caspian Sea and the breakaway republic of Chechnya.
Chernomyrdin issued a statement on Saturday pledging a full investigation. "I vouch that all necessary measures will be taken to uncover the reasons," his statement said.

President Boris Yeltsin, recovering from heart surgery, sent his condolences to relatives of the dead and the government said it would set up a commission under a deputy prime minister, Oleg Lobov, to investigate the causes of the blast.
Some officials have said there might be a link to the blast and Chechnya, where an ueasy peace is holding after a 21-month bloody conflict between Russian forces and separatists.

The Interior Ministry said it had not ruled out the possibility of a terrorist action, and Tass quoted official sources as saying it might be a revenge attack linked to a regional crackdown on arms and caviar smuggling.

Chechen rebel leader Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev, whose aide worked out a new draft agreement with Moscow on Saturday, on Sunday denied the separatists were involved in the blast, which he said was aimed at wrecking the peace process.
